categories.main_business_segments: Invesco Ltd. operates as a single integrated global investment management segment. The company provides comprehensive active, passive, and alternative investment capabilities across multiple asset classes including equities, fixed income, balanced, alternatives, and money market products. With approximately $1.6 trillion in assets under management as of December 31, 2023, Invesco serves clients in more than 120 countries through both retail and institutional distribution channels.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Invesco leverages specialized investment teams managing investments across diverse asset classes and geographies using distinct investment disciplines and risk management approaches. The company employs quantitative models for portfolio management, risk analysis, and client investment guidance. Key technology initiatives include the State Street Alpha platform, a single global investment operation engine being tested across asset classes. The company also utilizes advanced data analytics, digital wealth platforms, and technology infrastructure for portfolio management, trading, pricing, and client servicing.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Invesco serves both retail and institutional clients globally. Retail customers include individual investors accessing products through financial intermediaries, wire houses, broker-dealers, banks, and direct wealth platforms. Institutional clients include corporate entities, insurance companies, endowments, foundations, government authorities, universities, pension funds, and sovereign wealth funds. The company operates significantly in the U.S., Europe, Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific regions, with major presence in China through its Invesco Great Wall joint venture.
categories.geographic_coverage: Invesco maintains an on-the-ground presence in more than 20 countries with principal regional centers in the Americas (Houston and New York), EMEA (Henley-on-Thames, UK), and APAC (Hong Kong). The company serves clients in more than 120 countries. As of December 31, 2023, client domicile breakdown shows Americas at $1,133.9 billion (71.6%), EMEA at $215.9 billion (13.6%), and APAC at $235.5 billion (14.9%) of total AUM.
categories.supply_chain_position: Invesco operates as a midstream asset manager in the financial services supply chain. The company receives client assets for investment management, employs investment professionals to manage portfolios, and distributes investment products through various channels including retail intermediaries and direct institutional relationships. The company also provides ancillary services including fund administration, transfer agency, custody, and fiduciary services, positioning it as a comprehensive investment solutions provider.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Invesco's four key strategic objectives are: (1) Deliver excellence clients expect through strong long-term investment performance and superior client experience; (2) Grow high-demand investment offerings through product innovation and focus on high-opportunity markets; (3) Create an environment where talented people thrive through diversity and inclusive culture; (4) Act like owners for all stakeholders with disciplined resource stewardship. The company is simplifying operations, establishing unified platforms (fixed income, multi-asset, fundamental equity), and leveraging the State Street Alpha platform for operational efficiency and improved profitability.
categories.revenue_model: Invesco generates substantially all revenues from investment management contracts with clients. Revenue sources include: (1) Investment management fees based on assets under management (higher for active equity and alternatives, lower for passive and fixed income); (2) Service and distribution fees including transfer agency, administrative, and distribution fees; (3) Performance fees earned when certain performance metrics are achieved; (4) Other revenues from transaction fees and front-end fees. Investment management contracts are typically terminable with 30 or fewer days' notice.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Invesco competes with numerous investment management firms, commercial banks, investment banks, broker-dealers, hedge funds, insurance companies, and technology providers. Many competitors have greater financial resources and brand recognition. However, Invesco differentiates through its experience as a trusted partner, quality and diversity of investment capabilities, broad product range, multiple distribution channels, and independence as a standalone investment manager avoiding conflicts inherent in integrated financial institutions. The company is among the largest asset managers globally and ranks among leading managers in U.S. retail and EMEA retail markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Invesco is a large-scale global asset manager with approximately $1.6 trillion in AUM as of December 31, 2023, compared to $1.4 trillion at December 31, 2022 (12.5% increase). The company reported operating revenues of $5.7 billion in 2023 (down 5.5% from $6.0 billion in 2022) and net revenues of $4.3 billion (down 7.2% from $4.6 billion in 2022). Net income attributable to Invesco was a loss of $333.7 million in 2023 versus income of $683.9 million in 2022, primarily due to a $1.2 billion intangible asset impairment. Adjusted net income was $689.7 million in 2023 versus $773.2 million in 2022.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Invesco emphasizes delivering superior investment outcomes through proven strength of globally diverse investment teams with well-defined investment disciplines and risk management approaches. The company offers comprehensive solutions across active, passive, and alternative strategies with multiple investment objectives within various asset classes. Key differentiators include: (1) Breadth and depth of investment capabilities and vehicles; (2) Global diversification across asset classes, distribution channels, and geographies; (3) Independence avoiding conflicts of integrated institutions; (4) Quality client service and frictionless experience; (5) Innovation in product development and packaging; (6) Strong long-term investment performance; (7) Integrated global approach to risk management and operational excellence.
